lines.text: Today you are the art director. AI is your artist, and you decide exactly what it should draw.
First say the subject: who or what is in the picture and what they are doing.
Then choose a style, like cartoon, watercolour, poster art or paper-cut.
Lighting sets the mood, like a sunny morning or glowing festival lights.
Pick two or three colours that match your event and your club.
Composition says where things go, like leaving space for a title at the top.
AI learned from pictures made by people, so it can repeat unfair patterns.
Ask it to draw a doctor or an engineer four times and notice who appears.
Then write prompts that include everyone, whatever their gender or background.
Do not copy famous characters or logos that belong to other people.
Never make fake pictures of real people, like a cricket star or a classmate.
Always add a small label that says the image was made with AI.
This prompt names the subject, the style, the lighting, the colours and the layout.
Because we asked for empty space at the top, there is room to add our own title in Canva.
Now a bias check: we ask for a doctor several times and look at who appears.
If the pictures keep showing the same kind of person, the AI is repeating a pattern from its data.
We fix it by describing exactly who we want, so our poster includes everyone.
The picture looks great, but the AI has misspelled almost every word on it.
Image tools often get text wrong, so we ask for no text and add our own words in Canva.
In Canva, add your picture to a poster, then type the title, day, time and place yourself.
Check every detail, add a small “Image made with AI” label, and download it.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
